source_text: Καὶ ὁ Παῦλος δ᾿ ἐν τῇ πρὸς Θεσσαλονικεῖς ἐπιστολῇ δευτέρᾳ ἀποφαίνεται. τίνα τρόπον ἀποκαλυφθήσεταί ποτε „ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ ὑπεραιρόμενος ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα, ὥστ᾿ αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσαι, ἀποδεικνύοντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἐστὶ θεός.“ καὶ πάλιν φησὶ τοῖς Θεσσαλονικεῦσι· „καὶ νῦν τὸ κατέχον οἴδατε, εἰς τὸ ἀποκαλυφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ καιρῷ. τὸ γὰρ μυστήριον ἤδη ἐνεργεῖται τῆς ἀνομίας, μόνον ὁ κατέχων ἄρτι ἕως ἐκ μέσου γένηται· καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος, ὃν κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἀνελεῖ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, οὗ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν τοῦ σατανᾶ ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις καὶ τέρασι ψεύδους καὶ ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ ἀδικίας ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις.“ ἐκτιθέμενος δὲ καὶ τὴν αἰτίαν τοῦ ἐπιτρέπεσθαι τὸν ἄνομον ἐπιδημεῖν τῷ βίῳ φησίν· „ἀνθ᾿ ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς. καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμπει αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς ἐνέργειαν πλάνης εἰς τὸ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς τῷ ψεύδει. ἵνα κριθῶσιν ἅπαντες οἱ μὴ πιστεύσαντες τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ἀλλ᾿ εὐδοκήσαντες ἐν τῇ ἀδικίᾳ.“ λεγέτω τις οὖν ἡμῖν. εἰ δύναταί τι τῶν ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ ἢ τῶν παρὰ τῷ ἀποστόλῳ χώραν παρέχειν ὑπονοίας γοητείας προαγορευομένης κατὰ τὸν τόπον. παρέσται δὲ τῷ βουλομένῳ καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ Δανιὴλ ἐκλαβεῖν τὴν περὶ τοῦ ἀντιχρίστου προφητείαν. καταψεύδεται δὲ τῶν λόγων Ἰησοῦ, ἐπεὶ μὴ εἰπόντος αὐτοῦ· διότι παρέσονται ἕτεροι δυνάμεσιν ὁμοίαις χρώμενοι, κακοὶ καὶ γόητες, αὐτός φησιν αὐτὸν εἰρηκέναι τὸ τοιοῦτον. ὡς γὰρ οὐχ ὁμοία δύναμις ἡ τῶν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ ἐπαοιδῶν τῇ ἐν τῷ Μωϋσεῖ παραδόξῳ χάριτι, ἀλλὰ τὸ τέλος διήλεγχε τὰ μὲν τῶν Αἰγυπτίων ὄντα μαγγανείας τὰ δὲ τοῦ Μωϋσέως θεῖα· οὕτως τὰ μὲν τῶν ἀντιχρίστων καὶ τῶν προσποιουμένων δυνάμεις ὡς μαθητῶν Ἰησοῦ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα λέγεται εἶναι „ψεύδους.“ „ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ ἀδικίας τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις“ ἰσχύοντα, τὰ δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καρπὸν ἔσχεν οὐκ ἀπάτην ἀλλὰ σωτηρίαν ψυχῶν. Τίς γὰρ τὸν κρείττονα βίον καὶ συστέλλοντα τὰ τῆς κακίας ὁσημέραι ἐπὶ τὸ ἔλαττον εὐλόγως φησὶν ἀπὸ ἀπάτης γίνεσθαι;
pass_a_gloss: And Paul in the second letter (ἐπιστολή) to the Thessalonians declares (ἀποφαίνομαι) in what manner (τρόπος) will be revealed (ἀποκαλύπτω) at some time 'the man of lawlessness (ἀνομία), the son of destruction (ἀπώλεια), the one opposing (ἀντίκειμαι) and exalting himself (ὑπεραίρομαι) against every so-called god or object of reverence (σέβασμα), so that he sits in the temple (ναός) of God, showing (ἀποδείκνυμι) himself that he is God.' And again he says to the Thessalonians: 'and now you know the restraining [thing] (τὸ κατέχον), so that he is revealed in his own time (καιρός). For the mystery (μυστήριον) of lawlessness is already working (ἐνεργέομαι); only the restrainer (ὁ κατέχων) now until he comes out of the midst; and then will be revealed the lawless one (ὁ ἄνομος), whom the Lord God (κύριος ὁ θεός) will take away/slay (ἀναιρέω) with the breath/spirit (πνεῦμα) of his mouth and will abolish (καταργέω) by the manifestation (ἐπιφάνεια) of his coming (παρουσία), of whom the coming is according to the working (ἐνέργεια) of Satan in all power and signs and wonders of falsehood (ψεῦδος) and in all deceit (ἀπάτη) of unrighteousness in those perishing (ἀπόλλυμαι).' And setting out the cause (αἰτία) of the lawless one being permitted (ἐπιτρέπω) to sojourn (ἐπιδημέω) in life (βίος) he says: 'because they did not receive the love (ἀγάπη) of the truth so that they be saved (σῴζω). And for this God sends them a working of error (πλάνη) so that they believe the lie (ψεῦδος), in order that all be judged (κρίνω) who did not believe the truth but were well pleased (εὐδοκέω) in unrighteousness.' Let someone tell us then whether anything of those in the gospel or of those in the apostle (ἀπόστολος) can give room for suspicion (ὑπόνοια) of sorcery being foretold (προαγορεύω) in the passage. It will be possible for the one wishing to take also from Daniel the prophecy about the antichrist (ἀντίχριστος). And he lies against (καταψεύδομαι) the words of Jesus, since though he did not say 'that others will come using similar powers, evil men and sorcerers', he himself says that he said such a thing. For as not similar was the power of the enchanters (ἐπαοιδοί) in Egypt to the wondrous grace (παράδοξος χάρις) in Moses, but the end (τέλος) proved (διελέγχω) those of the Egyptians to be trickeries (μαγγανεία) and those of Moses divine, so the [works] of the antichrists and of those pretending (προσποιέομαι) powers as disciples of Jesus are said to be signs and wonders 'of falsehood', strong 'in all deceit of unrighteousness for those perishing', but those of Christ and his disciples had fruit (καρπός) not deceit but salvation (σωτηρία) of souls. For who reasonably (εὐλόγως) says that the better life and the one contracting (συστέλλω) the things of wickedness daily (ὁσημέραι) to less comes from deceit?
pass_b_english: Paul too, in the Second Letter to the Thessalonians, declares how there will one day be revealed “the man of lawlessness, the son of destruction, who opposes and exalts himself against every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, presenting himself as God” (2 Thessalonians 2:3–4). And again he says to the Thessalonians: “And now you know what restrains, so that he may be revealed in his own time. For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who now restrains will do so until he is taken out of the way. And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord God will slay with the breath of his mouth and will destroy by the appearing of his coming. The lawless one’s coming is by the working of Satan, with all power and signs and lying wonders, and with all the deceit of unrighteousness among those who are perishing” (2 Thessalonians 2:6–10). Setting out also the reason why the lawless one is allowed to come into this life, he says: “Because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved. And for this reason God sends them a working of error, so that they believe the lie, in order that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness” (2 Thessalonians 2:10–12).

Let someone tell us, then, whether anything in the Gospel or in the apostle can give ground for suspecting that sorcery is being foretold in this passage. Anyone who wishes may also draw from Daniel the prophecy about the antichrist (compare Daniel 7:24–26; 8:23–25; 11:36). But Celsus falsifies the words of Jesus: though Jesus did not say, “others will come using similar powers, wicked men and sorcerers,” Celsus himself says that he said such a thing. For just as the power of the enchanters in Egypt was not like the wondrous grace in Moses, but the outcome proved that the works of the Egyptians were trickery while those of Moses were divine (Exodus 7:10–12; 8:18–19), so the works of the antichrists, and of those who make a show of mighty works as though they were disciples of Jesus, are said to be signs and wonders “of falsehood” (2 Thessalonians 2:9), prevailing “with all the deceit of unrighteousness for those who are perishing” (2 Thessalonians 2:10); whereas the works of Christ and of his disciples bore as their fruit not deceit but the salvation of souls. For who could reasonably say that a better life, one that day by day reduces wickedness, comes from deceit?

2 Thess 2:9 οὗ: 'His coming' (ambiguous with the Lord's) -> 'The lawless one's coming'

translator_notes: 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4: Origen reads ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας (‘man of lawlessness’), the reading of Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (many manuscripts have ἁμαρτίας, ‘sin’). In 2:8 Origen’s text has κύριος ὁ θεός (‘the Lord God’) where the New Testament manuscripts read ‘the Lord’ or ‘the Lord Jesus’; translated as Origen’s text stands. Koetschau’s punctuation before τίνα τρόπον is treated as a misprint for an indirect question. The Daniel reference is a general pointer, not a quotation; the antichrist passages Origen elsewhere draws on are in Daniel 7-8 and 11, so the citation is marked ‘compare’. Celsus’s misquotation (‘others will come using similar powers, wicked men and sorcerers’) repeats his words from 2.49 and is put in quotation marks; the subject of καταψεύδεται is Celsus. Egyptian enchanters (ἐπαοιδοί, the LXX word in Exodus 7:11, 22): the outcome that exposed them is Aaron’s rod swallowing theirs (Exodus 7:10-12) and their failure with the gnats (Exodus 8:18-19 English = LXX 8:14-15; the Hebrew/LXX verse numbering in Exodus 8 runs four lower than the English, here given in English numbering). ‘Lying wonders’ keeps the Pauline genitive τέρασι ψεύδους; in the later echo it is rendered ‘of falsehood’ to keep Origen’s isolated quotation. Reviewer: Daniel 8:23-25 added to the ‘compare’ pointer; it is the antichrist passage Origen quotes at length in 6.46.
